subject.title: [Feature]: Supports Windows 11 MSYS environment and Fishshell.

question: Should OpenClaw officially support `install.sh` under Windows MSYS2/MINGW with fish-shell PATH handling, or keep Windows installs limited to Windows Hub, PowerShell, and WSL2?
rationale: The source change is mechanically plausible, but it expands the Windows installer support boundary and needs real Windows shell smoke coverage before automation should choose the behavior.

options.title: Support MSYS2 and fish
options.body: Approve MSYS2/MINGW `install.sh` support with fish-aware PATH handling, docs, focused tests, and real Windows smoke proof before merge.

options.title: Document unsupported shells
options.body: Keep Windows Hub, PowerShell, and WSL2 as the supported Windows paths and add explicit MSYS2/fish caveats to installer docs.

options.title: Defer to Windows tracker
options.body: Leave this issue open under the broader Windows platform tracker until platform owners decide the support boundary.

recommendation.title: Support MSYS2 and fish
recommendation.body: Approve MSYS2/MINGW `install.sh` support with fish-aware PATH handling, docs, focused tests, and real Windows smoke proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has the strongest recent source and docs history across the installer and Windows support wording.
